{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVlzVyc8AAAABd7J7aQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BqjeczhHcP_8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bqjec", "number": 18, "title": "refactor: extract shared action planning, approval, and evidence helpers", "body": "## Problem

The completed [tool architecture decision (Issue #16)](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/issues/16) sets a direction toward a small, composable set of general-purpose coding tools. Its [ordered roadmap, milestone 1](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/tool-architecture.md#ordered-implementation-roadmap), calls for extracting **shared action-plan, approval, and execution-evidence helpers** before implementing a versioned general patch contract or expanding command permissions.

Today, `apply_patch`, `create_file`, and `run_command` already enforce important but partly repeated preparation, preview/approval, cancellation, result reporting, and evidence ownership requirements in the Rust runtime and command pipeline. Further tool extensions without first consolidating the shared orchestration would duplicate policy and increase the risk of inconsistent behavior.

## Expected outcome

Refactor the **existing Rust implementation**, with the smallest coherent set of internal helpers, so current mutating file tools and approved command execution share appropriate action-lifecycle building blocks:

1. Validate/request and prepare an action under the current capabilities, without side effects during preview.
2. Present an immutable, correctly escaped and bounded description of the action and seek **explicit default-No** approval through the existing terminal callback.
3. Revalidate action-specific state before an irreversible operation; keep filesystem and sandbox enforcement in their existing dedicated backends.
4. Perform the action with the established cancellation and ownership rules.
5. Record truthful, structured outcomes in the existing in-memory ledger and CLI report.

Shared abstractions should cover only **truly common** behavior (approval invocation, preview/decision handling, lifecycle orchestration, evidence helpers as justified); retain safe operation-specific `openat`/`linkat`/patch publication, read-hash validation, and macOS Seatbelt command execution. Prefer a modest internal refactor over introducing a second runtime, complex framework, or speculative v2 types.

**No user-visible behavior change is intended.** The existing five model-facing tool contracts and their exact argument schemas must remain compatible. This milestone is a prerequisite for later general patch/execution work, not that work itself.

## Context and reproduction

- Current `main` at `ac0518a5b7d7b18244fe457c415a660038f3835b`.
- [Architecture decision / milestone 1](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/tool-architecture.md#ordered-implementation-roadmap).
- [`src/runtime.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/src/runtime.rs): root-anchored file operations, user approvals, tracked modifications and tool events.
- [`src/commands.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/src/commands.rs): exact-argv command allowlist, sandbox, bounded execution and cancellation.
- [`src/schema.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/src/schema.rs) and [`src/agent.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/src/agent.rs): closed schemas, ordered tool dispatch, error feedback and reporting.
- [Implementation/security reference](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/implementation.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), and [testing principles](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/testing-ci-principles.md).

This is a maintainability/safety refactor rather than a single broken user workflow; reproduction is not applicable.

## Mandatory pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **AC1 — Identify shared and distinct responsibilities:** Review current `apply_patch`, `create_file`, and `run_command` paths and identify repeated preparation, preview/approval, cancellation, and evidence management. Implement only justified shared Rust helpers. Document why operation-specific file and command security mechanisms remain distinct.
- [ ] **AC2 — Preserve approval/preview semantics:** Existing edit and new-file previews (diff, path, byte limits, sanitized terminal output) and exact argv command previews continue to appear before any side effect. Every mutation or command still requires a separate explicit `y`/Enter approval, defaulting to denial on blank input, EOF, cancellation or other answers. The caller cannot bypass approval through an alternate tool or shared helper.
- [ ] **AC3 — Preserve safety invariants and side effects:** Existing project-root confinement, `.git` and symlink protections, no-clobber file creation, read-hash/stale-state checks, existing-parent requirement, file-size limits and macOS sandbox/exact-command-allowlist behavior remain unchanged. No unsandboxed retry, command write permission, directory creation, delete/rename, or network capability is added.
- [ ] **AC4 — Preserve truthful evidence:** Existing JSON tool statuses/results, `executed` flags, SHA-256 and modified-file bookkeeping, command check outcomes, tool-call IDs/order, and final CLI reporting remain semantically compatible. Record committed side effects before later fallible/cancellation points. Denied/unrun work must never be reported as executed or passed; preserve previously committed edits after cancellation.
- [ ] **AC5 — Preserve failure, race and cancellation behavior:** Regression tests verify rejection before approval for invalid inputs where currently required, deny/EOF behavior, cancellation before and after file publication, stale state and destination races, and commands that fail, time out or are canceled. Tests must cover that shared abstractions do not weaken per-tool policy or leave unowned temporary effects.
- [ ] **AC6 — Test and validate on supported paths:** Run relevant deterministic Rust tests (including `tests/create_file.rs`, runtime, agent, command and CLI tests), plus the supported real-macOS security/sandbox regressions, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and applicable docs/whitespace checks. Report exact outcomes and unperformed checks; do not claim CI or real-hardware runs that were not performed.
- [ ] **AC7 — Compatibility and review scope:** Keep the five existing model-facing tool names and schemas, CLI flags, startup/launcher behavior, and Ollama tool-calling protocol unchanged. Update `docs/implementation.md` only as needed to describe shared internals, and reference the architecture roadmap. Make the refactor independently reviewable and revertible without affecting the later v2 parser or write-capable command milestones.

## Validation already performed

**Pass (repository inspection):** Reviewed current `main`, existing Issues, `src/schema.rs`, and [the architecture roadmap](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/tool-architecture.md#ordered-implementation-roadmap). No duplicate issue for roadmap milestone 1 was present.

**Not run:** Runtime refactor, regression suites, formatting, Clippy and live macOS checks. These remain implementation work, not results of Issue creation.

## Optional validation

Compare representative pre-/post-refactor terminal approval transcripts and tool-result JSON snapshots for edit, create and command cases. A real Ollama model trial is optional because model-facing contracts do not change in this milestone.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.
